Publisher XML full text converted with jats_text (section and paragraph locators)
pages_convention: XML section and paragraph locators (jats_text); figure-content steps and the Highlights box (PDF only) cite printed journal pages (319-331)

entry.evidence: raised concerns on the possible source of seismic events, whether the events could be precursors to a major earthquake

sequences.source_document: Sitali et al. 2022, J Seismol 26:319-331 (XML text and PDF)

steps.action: Five moderate earthquakes (4.0 < ML < 4.6) in May 2018 near Anker, recorded by the GSN permanent network, and felt events reported by the community since early 2018, are taken as the starting observation.
steps.quote: The recent occurrence of five moderate earthquakes recorded by the Namibian Seismological Network with magnitudes (4.0 < ML < 4.6) in May 2018

steps.action: The authors pose the question of the source of the swarm in a region where faults are poorly mapped and no local stations existed.
steps.quote: In order to understand the source of this seismic activity

steps.action: Rival swarm drivers from the literature are listed: fault creep, fluid or magmatic events, and small transient stress changes in a crust near failure.
steps.quote: The occurrence of seismic swarms is often associated with response to fault creep, fluid or magmatic events

steps.action: The expectation, taken from other studies, that rupture mechanisms should match the regional tectonic stress field whatever the transient trigger is adopted.
steps.quote: the resulting rupture mechanism will however be consistent with the regional tectonic stress field

steps.action: A 10-station temporary array covering about 50 km × 50 km is designed from the spatial distribution of known seismicity, with geometry chosen to constrain locations and focal mechanisms.
steps.quote: The stations were installed in a 50 km × 50 km radius to have an accurate overlap of the network coverage

steps.action: The GSN and CGS deploy Trillium Compact 120s sensors during the ongoing swarm, from 20 June to 24 September 2018.
steps.quote: installed a temporary network of 10 seismic stations to monitor the events for 3 months from 20 June to 24 September 2018

steps.action: More than 1600 microseismic events are recorded inside the array.
steps.quote: More than 1600 microseismic events were recorded and located within the boundaries of the array

steps.action: Events are located with SEISAN, and magnitudes are computed with the Saunders et al. (2013) ML scale: ML -1.1 to 3.6, depths up to 15 km.
steps.quote: The recorded data were analysed using the SEISAN software (Ottemöller et al. 36) to determine the source parameters.

steps.action: The two NW-SE clusters in the initial locations are compared with Kaoko belt structures and aeromagnetic lineaments; the upper cluster follows the Kaoko trend.
steps.quote: The upper seismic cluster follows the direction of regional tectonic structures of the Kaoko mobile belt.

steps.action: A minimum 1-D P-velocity model is inverted with VELEST from events recorded by at least eight stations. The starting model is Midzi et al. (2010) with modified layer thicknesses, refined iteratively before a final joint inversion.
steps.quote: it was decided to recompute a new local 1-D velocity model in order to improve the earthquake locations

steps.action: Events are relocated by double difference (absolute P and S differential times) with the new model. The two clusters merge into one cluster at the southern position, and the depth profile shows three west-dipping clusters down to about 25 km.
steps.quote: The main change in the distribution of relocated events is the disappearance of the two separated clusters of events.

steps.action: The NW-SE trend of the relocated events is compared with the regional tectonic setting (Kaoko belt, a known seismic zone); the authors note that no local structural mapping exists to corroborate it.
steps.quote: There are no detailed structural mapping studies done for the study area to corroborate our observation

steps.action: First-motion focal mechanisms are computed with FOCMEC for events with at least eight clear polarities (Table 1). Normal faulting dominates, many solutions have a left-lateral strike-slip component, and a few are reverse.
steps.quote: Each event selected had at least eight clear polarities.

steps.action: The authors propose that the swarm is linked to the triple junction of the Kaoko and Damara belts, since no known fault can be tied to it.
steps.quote: it is possible that the events are linked to the regional triple junction due to the Kaoko and Damara mobile belts

steps.action: Fluid migration, magmatic activity and transient stress are set aside as swarm drivers, by assertion and with no evidence shown.
steps.quote: However, in this area, neither of those activities is evident.

steps.action: The focal mechanisms are compared with the expectation that ruptures follow the regional stress; the regional stresses are found predominant but cannot be tied to local structures.
steps.quote: Results from the focal mechanism analysis indicate that regional tectonic stresses are predominant

steps.action: Remaining rivals are listed: stress transfer within a fault set under heterogeneous stress, pre-existing weaknesses triggered by loading or unloading, non-optimally oriented faults, and block faulting.
steps.quote: events might be taking place on non-optimally oriented faults or are caused by block faulting

steps.action: The authors keep a hedged claim: a NW-SE trend consistent with the Kaoko belt, mixed mechanisms, and seismicity possibly from reactivation of pre-stressed faults. They state that the source still needs future work.
steps.quote: Seismicity might be linked to reactivation of pre-stressed faults within the region due to changes in stress conditions.

tree.answer: No; a single swarm, with no repeated cases used
Not tested; no robustness, uncertainty or independent check reported

end.claim: The relocated Anker swarm trends NW-SE, consistent with the Kaoko mobile belt, and shows mixed, mainly normal, mechanisms; it is tentatively attributed to reactivation of pre-stressed faults under regional tectonic stress, with the source left for future work.

decisive_move.sentence: Without the 10-station temporary network deployed during the live swarm, none of the locations, the velocity model or the mechanisms would exist.

gates.evidence: The array was placed from the distribution of known seismicity (§0 ¶1), not from a stated hypothesis. The alignment with the Kaoko belt is a post hoc comparison that the authors say cannot be corroborated by local mapping (§5 ¶3). Fluid and magmatic rivals are dismissed by assertion (§7 ¶1). Nothing was fixed before the data were seen.

novelty_claims.quote: The 2018 seismic swarm in Anker area is the first to be ever recorded in the Namibian seismology.
Due to the limited number of seismic events recorded in Namibia, there is no locally developed velocity model for use in earthquake location.
In this study, a new average crustal velocity model was computed for the Anker local area

limits:
1. Checks. v_checks is empty: the paper reports no reproduction, robustness test, synthetic or control test, uncertainty estimate, residuals or held-out data for the velocity model, the relocations or the mechanisms. The tighter clustering after relocation is read as improvement (§5 ¶2) but not tested, so it is coded as R, not V.
2. Sub-claim statuses. The catalogue and the 1-D velocity model are estimates without stated resolution or uncertainty (closest to estimate_with_resolution, but unmet). The NW-SE alignment with the Kaoko belt is a qualitative comparison (status: none). The predominance of normal faulting is a descriptive estimate (status: none).
3. Headline status. The source attribution is hedged ('might', 'may be either'). The authors defer the source question to future work, so best_explanation is generous; a coder could argue no_conclusion on the stated aim.
4. Inconsistent depths. Depths are reported as less than 20 km (§0), up to 15 km (§3 ¶2, §8), and 10-25 km after relocation (§5 ¶2). Figure 6b (p. 326) plots events to about 35 km. The paper does not reconcile these.
5. Magnetic lineaments. Whether the lineaments were mapped in this study or taken from an existing aeromagnetic interpretation is unclear (§0 ¶1 versus the Figure 3 caption).
6. Table 1 entries (inference). Table 1 lists several near-identical origin times with different locations and mechanisms (e.g. 21 June 16:05:37.8 twice). This suggests duplicate or multiple solutions; it is not explained.
7. Mechanism quality. Focal mechanisms rely on at least eight polarities from a 10-station network, with no quality ranking.
8. Missing analysis. The May 2018 ML 4+ events that prompted the study are not analysed.
9. Dismissed rivals. The exclusion of fluid and magmatic drivers rests on a statement, with no data shown.
10. Composition. Composition is none_fits. The walk is a single live-event case study (deploy, locate, compare with regional structure, interpret). There are no repeated independent traces (so not trace_series), no fitted regularity, and no crucial test.
11. Entry. The entry is coded as an anomaly: unexpected seismicity in a region not listed among Namibia's seismogenic zones (§3 ¶1). A coder could also code it as a problem.
12. Sources. No review file was supplied, so there is no review sequence.

disagreements.target: Mangongolo and Hutchins (2008), seismogenic zones of Namibia
disagreements.support: The temporary network recorded more than 1600 events in the Kamanjab/Anker region, which the earlier zonation omits; the authors attribute the omission to a lack of data at the time.
disagreements.quote: In their findings, the Kamanjab region is not mentioned and this may be due to lack of seismic data at the time.

disagreements.target: Midzi et al. (2010) 1-D velocity model used for routine GSN location
disagreements.support: A local VELEST minimum 1-D model is inverted from the swarm data and shown against the Midzi model in Figure 5; it is used to relocate the events.
disagreements.quote: However, for this study, because of the localised nature of the hypocentral distances for [...]

alternatives_considered.chosen: New local minimum 1-D velocity model from VELEST
alternatives_considered.alternatives: Midzi et al. (2010) South African model used routinely by GSN
alternatives_considered.reason: localised nature of the hypocentral distances; to improve locations

alternatives_considered.chosen: Starting model with upper-crust layers about 2 km and lower-crust layers 4-5 km thick
alternatives_considered.alternatives: Unmodified Midzi et al. (2010) layer thicknesses
alternatives_considered.reason: inversion solves only for velocities, not layer thickness; upper-crust velocities vary more

alternatives_considered.chosen: Only events located by at least eight stations
alternatives_considered.reason: to ensure accuracy in the results

alternatives_considered.chosen: Saunders et al. (2013) South African ML scale
alternatives_considered.reason: same scale currently used by the GSN in Namibia

alternatives_considered.chosen: Absolute P- and S-wave travel-time differences in double-difference relocation
Regional tectonic stress and reactivation of pre-existing or pre-stressed faults
